so no two sources can collide and the scatter is deterministic; it is exactly

    out[o, k, i] = grad[o, i] if indices[o, i] == k else 0

    idx_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    M,
    R: tl.constexpr,
    K: tl.constexpr,
    BK: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
    FULLK: tl.constexpr,

    pid_k = tl.program_id(1)
    rows = pid_m * R + tl.arange(0, R)
    cols = pid_k * BK + tl.arange(0, BK)

    if EVEN:
        g = tl.load(g_ptr + rows)
        idx = tl.load(idx_ptr + rows).to(tl.int32)
    else:
        rmask = rows < M
        g = tl.load(g_ptr + rows, mask=rmask, other=0)
        idx = tl.load(idx_ptr + rows, mask=rmask, other=0).to(tl.int32)

    vals = tl.where(cols[None, :] == idx[:, None], g[:, None], tl.zeros_like(g)[:, None])
    offs = rows[:, None] * K + cols[None, :]

    if FULLK:
        if EVEN:
            tl.store(out_ptr + offs, vals)
        else:
            tl.store(out_ptr + offs, vals, mask=rmask[:, None])
    else:
        if EVEN:
            tl.store(out_ptr + offs, vals, mask=cols[None, :] < K)
        else:

                out_ptr + offs,
                vals,
                mask=rmask[:, None] & (cols[None, :] < K),

    idx_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    N,
    INNER: tl.constexpr,
    K: tl.constexpr,
    GO_SPLIT: tl.constexpr,
    GO_ST0: tl.constexpr,
    GO_ST1: tl.constexpr,
    GI_SPLIT: tl.constexpr,
    GI_ST0: tl.constexpr,
    GI_ST1: tl.constexpr,
    IO_SPLIT: tl.constexpr,
    IO_ST0: tl.constexpr,
    IO_ST1: tl.constexpr,

Per-workload evidence shows two independent losses: (1) all small/medium workloads sit ~0.21 ms against a ~0.135 ms reference floor, i.e. two Triton launches each cost ~35 us of host walltime beyond the reference's aten calls; (2) the two largest workloads are element-rate rather than bandwidth bound - fp16 8192x8192 (134 MB) and fp32 8192x8192 (268 MB) both take ~0.739 ms (~90 Gelem/s), while the reference sustains ~417 GB/s on both (0.324/0.640 ms), so the fully masked store is not vectorized and costs a fixed per-element rate regardless of dtype.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: No prior measurement (baseline round). Absolute position: worst workload timing-2 at 0.4386x, best timing-14 at 0.865x. Reference latency is flat at ~0.135-0.15 ms for the 12 small/medium workloads (floor bound), so the recoverable loss there is host-launch overhead only; on the 6 large workloads the dtype-insensitive 0.739 ms is recoverable store-bandwidth.

The zero+scatter pair remains only for the non-last-dim / non-contiguous general path.
plan.hypothesis: The baseline lost for two separable reasons: two launches (host floor) and masked stores (element-rate). Fusing removes the second launch and the constexpr-K unmasked tile restores store vectorization, so fp16 large cases should approach the fp32 case's byte rate and all 12 floor-bound workloads should approach a 1.0x speedup.

        inner *= s

    n = out.numel()
    _zero_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n, _ZERO_BLOCK),)](out, n, BLOCK=_ZERO_BLOCK)

    g_shape = list(grad.shape)
    g_st = list(grad.stride())
    if len(g_shape) == nd:
        del g_shape[d]
        del g_st[d]
    i_st = list(indices.stride())
    if len(i_st) == nd:
        del i_st[d]

    go_split, go_st0, go_st1 = _group(g_shape[:d], g_st[:d])
    gi_split, gi_st0, gi_st1 = _group(g_shape[d:], g_st[d:])
    io_split, io_st0, io_st1 = _group(g_shape[:d], i_st[:d])
    ii_split, ii_st0, ii_st1 = _group(g_shape[d:], i_st[d:])

    ns = grad.numel()
    _scatter_general[(triton.cdiv(ns, _SCATTER_BLOCK),)](
        grad,
        indices,
        out,
        ns,
        INNER=inner,
        K=k,
        GO_SPLIT=go_split,
        GO_ST0=go_st0,
        GO_ST1=go_st1,
        GI_SPLIT=gi_split,
        GI_ST0=gi_st0,
        GI_ST1=gi_st1,
        IO_SPLIT=io_split,
        IO_ST0=io_st0,
        IO_ST1=io_st1,
        II_SPLIT=ii_split,
        II_ST0=ii_st0,
        II_ST1=ii_st1,
        BLOCK=_SCATTER_BLOCK,
    )
    return out

profile.summary: mixed: 15 of 18 timing workloads are pinned by a ~100 us per-call host floor, not by kernel time, fp16/bf16 large case is dominated by the per-element compare/select, not by store bandwidth, fp32 large case: no pipe is saturated (MTE2/MTE3 <80% when active, vector compute usage <20%) while effective write rate is 845 GB/s

conclusion.root_cause: The 0.59 baseline lost on two independent axes; fusing removed both the second launch and the masked-store element-rate wall, taking geo_mean to 1.5502 with 96/96 exact. Remaining loss is now localized: a per-call host cost of ~98-105 us that dominates 15 of 18 timing workloads, a ~845 GB/s DRAM write wall on the largest fp32 case (at it), and dtype-independent select compute (int32 compare + where) that holds fp16/bf16 8192^2 at 730 GB/s instead of ~845 GB/s.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: geo_mean 0.5905 -> 1.5502 (+162%), min_speedup 0.4386 -> 1.4462, all 96 workloads still exact. The fusion half of the hypothesis is fully confirmed: every floor-bound workload moved from ~0.21 ms to 0.098-0.108 ms, i.e. exactly max(H, T) with a single per-call host cost H ~= 98-105 us, and the two-launch penalty disappeared. The 'unmasked stores make large workloads bandwidth bound' half is only partially confirmed: timing-14 (fp32 8192^2, 268 MB) reached 845 GB/s and is at the practical HBM write wall for this single-die part (~2x the reference's 417 GB/s), but timing-2/timing-8 (fp16/bf16, 134 MB) reach only 730 GB/s because the [R,BK] int32 compare + tl.where costs 127.6 us of the 183.9 us kernel (MTE3 only 17% active), so those two remain select-compute bound. Profiler kernel times: timing-0 5.5 us, timing-16 11.4 us, timing-13 81.5 us, timing-2 183.9 us, timing-14 317.9 us - so 15 of 18 timing workloads are host-floor bound and cannot be moved by kernel changes.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Diagnose the ~98 us per-call host cost first (allocation vs Triton launch vs harness sync) because it gates 15 of 18 timing workloads; then try replacing the full-tile where-select with a zero-tile store plus a one-element scatter store to cut fp16/bf16 select compute.
conclusion.debug_lesson: Per-element select cost is dtype-independent (fp32 vec 141.5 us vs fp16 127.6 us for the same 67.1 M elements) while duration tracks bytes, so element-rate work and byte-rate work must be optimized separately.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: From a two-launch zeros+scatter mirror of aten to a single fused gather-formulation kernel with constexpr-K unmasked contiguous stores; next, attack the host per-call floor and the per-element select independently since they are the only two remaining limits.
